sheet-1-1.description: The main part of the title sheet of the 1923 Wrightstown atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It covers the centre of the borough east of South Street or Pemberton Road (today Fort Dix Street), from the frontage north of Main Street or Hanover Road south to Rexall Avenue and the lots beyond it, and east to the fork where Main Street divides into Cookstown Road (today East Main Street) and Hanover Road (today McGuire Air Force Base Road). The Philadelphia and Reading Railroad line operated by the Union Transportation Company crosses the sheet diagonally from south-west to north-east, with a passenger depot, a freight house, a coal trestle, a store house and the milk depot of the Supplee-Wills-Jones Milk Company along its sidings. Along South Street are small stores, a post office, a general storage building, a fire department house and dwellings. Between the railroad and Hanover Road lie the Davis Bros. grist mill and the pumping station and office of the Wrightstown Water, Electric Light and Sewer Company, with auto repair shops, and on Hanover Road the Jr. O.U.A.M. Hall. A public school stands north of Cookstown Road. The south-east edge of the block along Hanover Road is labelled as the boundary of the U.S. Government Reservation Camp Dix, and blocks there are marked vacant beyond. The sheet carries the title cartouche, the water-supply and fire-department notes, the legend and a small locator map of New Jersey, which is left out of the georeferenced area. Most of the drawn area is dwellings on deep lots with outbuildings, typical of a small crossroads town beside the army camp.
notes: Main Street or Hanover Road is today West Main Street and East Main Street; South Street or Pemberton Road is Fort Dix Street.
Cookstown Road is today East Main Street; Hanover Road follows the line of McGuire Air Force Base Road, whose north-west end no longer reaches East Main Street.
Rexall Avenue is approximately today's Railroad Avenue, which now runs on the old railroad land and curves into Fort Dix Street.
The railroad (P. & R.R.R., Union Transportation Co. lessee) is abandoned; its crossings of Main Street and South Street were used as control from the OpenStreetMap abandoned-railway line.
Main Street is drawn about 55 ft wide east of South Street and about 75 ft wide west of it, and jogs at the junction.

50 ft to an inch; title sheet with key, water and fire notes, and a locator map of New Jersey (cut out of the mask). Part 1: Main St or Hanover Rd (West/East Main Street) east of South St or Pemberton Rd (Fort Dix Street), the P. & R.R.R. (Union Transportation Co.) yard and depots, Rexall Av (today Railroad Avenue), and the fork of Cookstown Rd (East Main Street) and Hanover Rd (McGuire Air Force Base Road). Part 2 (below the heavy zigzag line, right of the vertical line): Cookstown Rd further east at an unnamed 20 ft Road (Edna Street), with a second Hanover Rd branching to the south-east whose line is lost in McGuire AFB; drawn displaced from part 1. Only one street junction survives per part; parts placed mostly from hand-picked parcel corners and former railroad crossings.

sheet-1-2.description: A separately placed part in the lower right of the title sheet, framed by a heavy line, showing Cookstown Road (today East Main Street) east of the railroad, roughly 250 to 450 metres east of South Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch but displaced on the page from the main part of the sheet. North of Cookstown Road, in block 4, a 20 ft unnamed road labelled only Road (today Edna Street) runs north between lots of two-and-a-half-storey dwellings with outbuildings, a blacksmith and auto repairing shop and gas tanks. South of Cookstown Road, in block 5, a second Hanover Road branches off to the south-east; between the two roads stand a large storage building, a vacant building, a lodging house, a work shop with an electric motor and several dwellings, numbered 201 to 209 along Hanover Road. The area south of Cookstown Road lies inside today's Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, and this Hanover Road has no modern counterpart. Ground beyond the drawn lots is marked as having no exposure. The compass rose and the scale bar of the sheet are drawn in this part.
notes: Cookstown Road is today East Main Street; the unnamed 20 ft Road is today Edna Street (identified from the lot pattern, which matches today's parcels north of East Main Street).
This Hanover Road, branching from Cookstown Road east of the main fork, is not in today's street network.
Placed from a single hand-picked junction (Cookstown Road / Road) and a derived point that sets the drawn Cookstown Road on the bearing of East Main Street; scale taken from part 1. Low confidence.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 of the 1923 Wrightstown atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It continues the town centre westward from sheet 1: Main Street or Hanover Road (today West Main Street) from South Street or Pemberton Road (today Fort Dix Street) west for about 300 metres, with the frontage on both sides, and the west side of South Street south to the railroad crossing and the end of Rexall Avenue. Along Main Street are dwellings on long lots, a lumber shed and a storage building for building material, a blacksmith and wheelwright, a Methodist church, the ruins of a burned building, a bank with a vault, an auto repair shop and a tenant garage. At the north-east corner of Main and South Streets stands a larger group of buildings with a brick store. The lots on the west side of South Street hold a few stores and vacant buildings, numbered 15 to 39 from the railroad to Main Street. The Philadelphia and Reading Railroad (Union Transportation Company, lessee) crosses South Street at the bottom right. Much of the block south of Main Street is open ground. The lower left and lower middle of the sheet are separate insets described in their own parts.
notes: Main Street or Hanover Road is today West Main Street; South Street or Pemberton Road is Fort Dix Street; Rexall Avenue is approximately Railroad Avenue.

Main Street is drawn about 75 ft wide here, wider than today's right-of-way; the south frontage and the rear line of the block south of Main Street match today's parcel lines, which were used as control.
The railroad is abandoned; its crossing of South Street was taken from the OpenStreetMap abandoned-railway line.

50 ft to an inch. Part 1: Main St or Hanover Rd (West Main Street) west of South St or Pemberton Rd (Fort Dix Street), and South St south to the railroad and Rexall Av. Part 2 (inset, lower left): Main St at Springfield Rd (Meeting House Road) and Jobstown Rd (Saylors Pond Road), with the water works pumping station and steel tank. Part 3 (inset, lower middle): South St or Pemberton Rd at its south end by the U.S. Govt Reservation Camp Dix, numbers 2 to 8; no cross street or shared feature, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: South St or Pemberton Rd (Fort Dix Street) at the Camp Dix boundary, house numbers 2 to 8 (no street junction and no feature shared with a placed part; the strip can be lined up across Fort Dix Street but not along it; needs a dated survey or aerial of the old Pemberton Road frontage at Fort Dix).

sheet-2-2.description: An inset in the lower left of sheet 2, framed by a heavy line, showing the west end of Wrightstown where Main Street or Hanover Road (today West Main Street) meets Springfield Road (today Meeting House Road), running to the north-west, and Jobstown Road (today Saylors Pond Road), running to the west-south-west. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and lies just west of the main part of the sheet. North of the junction, set back in an open lot, is the water works pumping station of the town supply, connected by a 4-inch water pipe to a 10,000 gallon steel water tank on a 75 ft tower beside Springfield Road. South of Main Street are a few dwellings with outbuildings, an ice house and a wood shed on deep lots; the ground to the north is marked no exposure. The inset has its own north arrow.
notes: Springfield Road is today Meeting House Road; Jobstown Road is today Saylors Pond Road; Main Street or Hanover Road is West Main Street.

Placed from the single junction of the three roads, with rotation from its drawn street lines and the scale of sheet 2; low confidence. The drawn roads lie on the modern roads in the check overlay, but lot lines do not match today's parcels.
